title: gemm_bias's mixed_magnitude tolerance is met by no fp32 accumulation order at all, only by accumulating in fp64, so the task cannot qualify on any target

evidence.retained: bw1100 /home/testuser01/oci-dcu-runs/gemm_bias-20260918-064243, four turns and a 400000 token budget, adhered with endpoint_observation no_qualified_candidate; and a CPU-only reproduction at the launcher's shape for this task (M=128, K=256, N=1024) using the Workload's own generator and its declared atol and rtol, with every accumulator held in fp32 and its dtype printed per row
sites: that run's correctness_output: participants.baseline.preflight.launches -- mixed_magnitude passed false, max_abs_error 0.09375, output_mismatches 27, while primary, zeros, near_zero and alternating all pass
the same document's candidate half fails the same case with the same 0.09375; the run's pooled output_mismatches is 54, 27 from each participant

the declared tolerance_rationale, verbatim: sized from the measured worst sequential-FP32 departure from an fsum oracle, '3.1e-2 absolute at outputs of order 2e5', and 'It is a numerical allowance, not device calibration'

measured on CPU over mixed_magnitude, every accumulator fp32: sequential 0.0855395 with 27 elements outside tolerance, torch matmul 0.0596697 with 21, split-K at widths 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64 between 0.0531135 and 0.08584 with 15 to 26; accumulating in fp64 and rounding once departs by 0.0154169 with 0 outside

the 27 elements sequential fp32 fails have |ref| between 2.67627 and 102.748, median 21.1299, with deviations 0.00201488 to 0.0186717 against allowances 0.00126763 to 0.0112748 -- cancellation survivors, not the large outputs
the same measurement on the primary case: every ordering passes, max departure 3.58e-05

observation:
The starter reference does not pass the Workload's own validation set on this target. mixed_magnitude is the case it fails -- signed powers of two from 2^-12 to 2^8, so a contraction over K accumulates terms spanning twenty binades -- and it fails by 0.09375 on 27 elements while the other four cases pass, primary at 6.87e-05. Two turns produced two different candidate digests and both were rejected on correctness with the identical error, which is the tell that the error is not the candidate's: Common Evaluation checks both participants against the oracle, so a candidate is being compared to a reference that is itself outside tolerance.

An earlier version of this record claimed the tolerance was met by strictly sequential fp32 and by nothing else, and concluded that it 'bounds the one order nothing uses'. That was wrong, and an independent reviewer caught it by reproducing the measurement rather than reading it. The error was in the probe: its sequential accumulator was built with torch.zeros_like(ref) where ref was float64, so it accumulated in fp64 and the figure reported for sequential fp32 -- 0.0154169, 0 elements outside -- is the fp64 row.

Redone with every accumulator held in fp32 and its dtype printed: sequential fp32 departs by 0.0855395 with 27 elements outside, which is the baseline's own failure. torch's matmul leaves 21 outside, and split-K at six widths leaves between 15 and 26. Nothing in fp32 passes. Accumulating in fp64 and rounding once passes with 0 outside, and that is not an accumulation order a GEMM uses -- it is the oracle.

So the claim is stronger than the one it replaces, not weaker: no fp32 accumulation order meets this case's elementwise tolerance, so the task cannot qualify on gfx938, on sm_103a, or on anything else contracting in fp32. That it was also reported failing on B300 is consistent with this and needs no separate cause.

Where the failures sit also corrects the earlier reading. They are not the large outputs: the 27 elements have |ref| between 2.68 and 102.7 with a median of 21.1, and deviations between 0.002 and 0.019 against allowances between 0.0013 and 0.0113. They are the elements where twenty binades of signed terms cancelled down to something small, so the absolute error survives while rtol buys almost nothing. The rationale's '3.1e-2 absolute at outputs of order 2e5' describes a magnitude that is not where this case fails.
proposed_change:
The Workload Contract owns this, and the fix is not the one this record proposed before. Re-deriving the allowance across blocked and split-K orders changes nothing, because sequential fp32 already fails by more than any of them: the allowance is not mis-sized against the wrong order, it is below what fp32 can deliver on this case at all.

Two shapes remain and the choice is the owner's. Narrow mixed_magnitude's exponent range so a contraction over K leaves fewer terms to cancel, which is what actually produces the surviving absolute error; or state the accumulation precision the case requires, since fp64 accumulation does meet the current allowance and an fp32 contraction cannot. The rationale should then describe where the case fails -- cancellation survivors of order 10, not outputs of order 2e5 -- because the magnitude it currently names is comfortably inside tolerance.

Still do not widen atol to make the case pass. The number to change is the one whose derivation is wrong, and changing it means redoing that derivation against fp32 arithmetic -- not raising a threshold until the observed failure fits under it.

No second target is needed: the reproduction is CPU-only and hardware-independent.
